task: pay a bill through a bank or biller portal (bank bill pay, utility, credit-card, phone-company sites): log in, locate the bill or add the payee, set the amount and payment date, pick the funding account, submit; complete when the payment-scheduled or payment-confirmed screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank's bill-pay interface or a biller's own web/app payment portal. Variants: setting up recurring autopay, sending money to a person, and paying at a store register do not belong.

tree.label: Pay a bill online
tree.note: 1 where the session is not already inside - half the keepers arrive signed in. then 2. 3 on the bill-pay and wallet surfaces, where the payee has to be found, linked or typed; on the issuer sites the To field is the user's own card or loan and 3 is skipped. 4 before 5, though on the wallet surfaces the bill is read at the form itself. 5, then 6 - or 6 first where the source has to be linked before anything (EnZK), or 6.2 mid-way when the picked account turns out unverified (W0JT). 7 where the platform offers dates and rails; on the wallets the money leaves at once, so 7 is only reading what the platform prints. then 8, then 9. 9.7 loops back to 2 for the next bill - three times in 8n6j.

children.label: Get into the account
children.note: 1.1 where the video starts outside the app or site, then 1.2; 1.3 whenever the platform interrupts. 1.4 once, on a bank whose bill pay is not yet enrolled (NfKb) or a tool that charges for it (W0JT). 1.5 in place of 1.2 on a biller portal that has never seen the user (RoGB) - the login page offers sign in, register, or a one-time payment by account number, and the first visit takes register.

questions.question: Which ways into the payment portal does the page offer?
questions.why: The screen offers options to log in with an email and password, register for a new account, or make a one-time payment using just an account number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice between the long-term convenience of a saved account profile and the privacy of a quick one-time guest payment.
questions.check: Which ways into the portal does the page offer - sign in, register, or pay as a guest with an account number?
questions.say_example: This site lets me pay with just the account number, no sign-in. You didn't give me a login, so I'm using that.

questions.question: Which app on the screen is the bank's or biller's own?
questions.why: The screen displays a folder with multiple finance apps, so you must identify the correct bank or biller app to initiate the payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific bank or financial institution to use for managing and paying their bills.
questions.check: Which app on the screen carries the bank's or biller's own name?
questions.say_example: Opened <the bank app>

questions.question: Which search result is the bank's real site?
questions.why: The top search result is an ad, so selecting the second link ensures you reach the legitimate S-Pankki site instead of a potentially misleading sponsored link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of personally verifying that the authentic, non-sponsored bank link was chosen to avoid phishing risks.
questions.check: Is the top search result marked as an ad or sponsored, and which result is the bank's own domain?
questions.say_example: The first result is an ad. The real <bank> site is the second one, so I'm using that.

questions.question: Is your biller on the list of supported companies shown on the landing page?
questions.why: The landing page outlines benefits like instant payments and displays logos of the 13 supported companies so you know what is available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to learn about the platform's features and verify if your specific biller is supported before logging in.
questions.check: Does the list of supported billers on the landing page include the biller on your bill?
questions.say_example: This site lists <13> billers it can pay. <Your biller> isn't one of them. It can't pay this bill. I'll look for the biller's own site.

questions.question: Will you type your bank username and password in yourself?
questions.why: The login page requires a username and password to proceed with the selected passcode table method.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must share their sensitive banking credentials with the agent to allow it to log in.
questions.check: Which sign-in fields does the page show, which are still empty, and does the page say what a first-time password is made of?
questions.say_example: The bank wants your username and password. I don't take those. Type them in, and tell me when you're through.

questions.question: Will you choose and type the new password the site now requires?
questions.why: The portal requires you to create a new 4-6 digit password before you can finish logging in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose a memorable, secure password that you alone know for future access to this account.
questions.check: Does the page require a new password to be created now, and what rules does it list for it?
questions.say_example: It won't let you in until you set a new password. <Four to six digits>. Choose one and type it yourself. I'll wait.

questions.question: Will you enter the second code from your phone, app, or passcode table yourself?
questions.why: The login screen requires a secondary authentication code sent via SMS to verify your identity before granting access to the portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires giving the agent real-time access to your personal text messages to complete the multi-factor authentication.
questions.check: What second-step code does the page ask for - a text message, an app, or a printed passcode table - and which cell or number does it name?
questions.say_example: It wants the code from the text it just sent you. Read it to me, or type it in yourself.

questions.question: Are the remember-username and Face ID toggles left off?
questions.why: The login screen includes toggles for 'Remember Username' and 'Enable Face ID Authentication' that determine how easily the account can be accessed later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal choice of balancing convenience and device-level security by deciding whether to store credentials or use biometrics.
questions.check: Are the 'Remember Username' and 'Enable Face ID' toggles on or off?
questions.say_example: Left Face ID and remember-me off

questions.question: Is the account type in the login dropdown the right one for your account?
questions.why: The login form requires your User ID, password, and the correct account type selection from the dropdown to successfully access your billing account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the correct account type is selected from the dropdown before submitting your login credentials.
questions.check: Which account type is selected in the dropdown on the login form?
questions.say_example: The login form is set to <business>. Your account is <personal>, so I'm switching it before I sign in.

questions.question: Does the page say the account is locked?
questions.why: Security policies, expired credentials, or too many failed login attempts by an agent can trigger a lockout or forced reset, preventing access to the bill pay dashboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally recover their account, answer security questions, or update their credentials securely when the standard login flow is interrupted.
questions.check: Does the page say the account is locked after too many tries?
questions.say_example: The bank says this account is locked after too many tries. I can't get past that. You'll need to unlock it with them first.

questions.question: Is a CAPTCHA or picture puzzle blocking the login?
questions.why: Many bank portals use visual challenges like selecting images to prevent automated logins, which must be solved to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might fail silently or get stuck in a loop if it cannot interpret or solve a purely visual security challenge.
questions.check: Is there a CAPTCHA or picture challenge on the login page?
questions.say_example: There's a picture puzzle to prove you're a person. I'm not going to solve it. Do it and tell me when it's through.

questions.question: Do you want to extend your banking session before it times out?
questions.why: The screen displays a 60-second warning that your session will expire for security reasons unless you choose to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to quickly intervene to keep the session active, risking a timeout and lost progress if the agent misses the brief warning window.
questions.check: Is a session timeout warning showing with a continue button?
questions.say_example: Kept the session alive at the <60 second> warning

children.label: Enroll in the bill-pay service
children.note: 1.4.1 alone on a bank (NfKb). 1.4.2, then 1.4.3, then 1.4.4 on the paid tool (W0JT); 6.2.3 follows before the first payment can be made.

questions.question: Do you want to hear the Bill Pay Agreement before I accept it?
questions.why: The screen requires agreeing to a legal contract that covers your rights and responsibilities for the digital banking services before you can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read and understand the specific legal terms, rights, and responsibilities you are legally binding yourself to.
questions.check: Which agreement does the page require accepting before continuing, and what does it say about fees, liability, or cancellation?
questions.say_example: Before it lets you pay, the bank wants you to accept its Bill Pay Agreement. Want me to read the main points, or say accept.

questions.question: Which bill-pay plan do you want, given each one is a monthly charge?
questions.why: The screen presents three subscription tiers with different monthly costs and ACH payment limits that dictate your ongoing business expenses.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose the subscription tier that best balances the monthly fee with your expected payment volume.
questions.check: Which plans does the page list, and what monthly price and payment limit does each show?
questions.say_example: Three plans. <Basic> is <15> a month with <5> free payments. <Elite> is <90> a month plus <1.27> per check. This is a charge every month. Which one?

questions.question: Are the business name and address on the form the ones you gave me?
questions.why: The screen displays a business profile setup form with pre-filled data and address suggestions that must be verified to enroll in the service.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify or correct their business information before it is submitted for enrollment.
questions.check: Does the business name and address on the form match what you gave me, and is the page suggesting a different address?
questions.say_example: The form filled in <an old address>. That's not the one you gave me, so I'm correcting it.

questions.question: Do you want to give your SSN, date of birth, and home address for the identity check?
questions.why: The form requires sensitive personal details, including the last 4 digits of your SSN and your date of birth, to verify your identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your ability to control exactly when and where your highly sensitive personal information is shared for underwriting purposes.
questions.check: Which identity fields does the form require - SSN digits, date of birth, home address?
questions.say_example: To turn on bill pay, the site wants the last four of your SSN and your date of birth. That's for identity checks. Type them yourself, or say skip and we stop here.

questions.question: Did the 'About you' section save and unlock the next step?
questions.why: The 'About you' section is still marked 'In progress' and the 'Your payment method' section remains greyed out and collapsed, indicating the form submission silently failed or stalled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to recognize that their personal information was not accepted, leaving them stuck in the setup flow.
questions.check: Does the 'About you' section show as complete, or still 'In progress' with the next section greyed out?
questions.say_example: The form says it saved, but the section still shows in progress and the next step is locked. I'm trying it again.

questions.question: Are you okay waiting up to three business days for the micro-deposits to verify your account?
questions.why: The modal states that two small deposits will be made to your account within three business days to complete the verification process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your funding account is not instantly available and will require manual follow-up to verify the deposits.
questions.check: What does the page say about how the account is verified, and how long it takes?
questions.say_example: The site verifies your bank with two tiny deposits. That takes up to three business days. Your bill is due <date>, so it won't be paid from here before then.

questions.question: What account number from your statement does the registration ask for?
questions.why: The screen requires you to enter the account number found on your statement to identify your account and continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to keep your specific utility account number private from the agent.
questions.check: What number does the registration form ask for, and where does the page say it is printed?
questions.say_example: To register it needs the account number from your paper statement. Top right, the page says. Read it to me.

questions.question: Will you pick the security question and type its answer yourself?
questions.why: The screen requires you to provide contact information and select a security question to establish your account access.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent chooses your security questions and profile details, which could make it difficult for you to recover or access the account later.
questions.check: Which security question is selected, and is the answer field empty?
questions.say_example: It wants a security question and answer. Those recover the account later, so I shouldn't know them. Pick one and type the answer, then tell me.

questions.question: Is the service address shown the one for the account you're paying?
questions.why: The portal requires you to verify your identity by confirming that the partially hidden service address matches your records before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that the retrieved service address matches your own before confirming the payee.
questions.check: What partially hidden service address does the page ask you to confirm?
questions.say_example: It's asking whether <a partly hidden address on Oak St> is your service address. If that's not your place, say stop.

children.label: Reach the payment
children.note: 2.1 first on the issuer and bank sites; 2.2 on any dashboard with more than one account or bill. 2.3 on the bill-pay and wallet surfaces, 2.4 on all of them - 2.4 is the PAY button on the account row, the Make a payment on a payee, or the arrow beside a biller. EnZK runs 2.4 twice, before and after 6.2.

questions.question: Does the available balance shown cover the bill you are about to pay?
questions.why: The screen displays your available balance of 5 500,00 EUR and recent account activity, which is crucial for verifying you have sufficient funds before initiating a bill payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally audit your recent spending and ensure all listed transactions are accurate and authorized.
questions.check: What available balance does the summary show, and what is the bill amount?
questions.say_example: Your available balance is <120>. The bill is <217>. Paying it would overdraw you. I'm holding.

questions.question: Which of the listed accounts or bills is the one to pay?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple accounts with varying balances and due dates, requiring you to select the specific obligation you intend to pay.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to prioritize which specific debt or bill to pay based on your current financial strategy.
questions.check: Which accounts or bills does the page list, with what balance and due date for each?
questions.say_example: Three cards here. <Discover>, <251.81> due <the 15th>. <Visa>, <60> due <the 20th>. <Amex>, nothing due. Which one are we paying?

questions.question: Is this the 'Pay bills' screen, not 'Bill', which records the bill and pays nothing?
questions.why: The '+ New' menu presents multiple vendor-related actions like 'Expense', 'Check', and 'Bill', so you must specifically select 'Pay bills' to access the correct payment workflow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review other available vendor transaction types that might be relevant to your current accounting needs.
questions.check: Which menu item is highlighted - 'Pay bills', or 'Bill', 'Check', or 'Expense'?
questions.say_example: This menu has 'Bill' and 'Pay bills'. 'Bill' only records it. Nothing gets paid. I'm on 'Pay bills'.

questions.question: Has the phone number you're paying been unused for more than three months?
questions.why: The screen provides a specific alternative link that must be used to successfully make a payment if the target phone number has been inactive for over three months.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to direct the agent to the correct alternative payment flow for an inactive account, risking a failed transaction.
questions.check: Does the page say a number inactive for over three months needs a different link?
questions.say_example: The page says a number unused for three months needs a different form. I'm assuming yours is active. Say so if it isn't.

questions.question: Do you still want to pay when the minimum due is zero?
questions.why: The screen shows a $0.00 minimum payment due, but paying now prevents interest from accruing on the remaining balance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the financial foresight to proactively pay down a balance and avoid interest when an agent might just skip the payment upon seeing zero dollars due.
questions.check: What minimum payment does the page show, and what is the full balance?
questions.say_example: Minimum due is <0>. The balance is still <217>, and interest builds on it. I'm paying the <balance> you asked for.

children.label: Identify the payee
children.note: skipped on the issuer sites, where the To field is the user's own card or loan (B3DP, Nu5a, VmJW, 8n6j, Kgwb, KUG3, b_Qz, EnZK). 3.1 then 3.2 on the wallets; 3.2 then 3.4 or 3.5 on the bank bill-pay surfaces when the directory misses; 3.3 in place of all of it when the payee is on file - dlQH backs out of a blank form to take a favorite. 3.5 on S-Pankki with no directory at all. 3.6 as a detour (NfKb) or as the check after 3.5.5 (4uIk).

questions.question: Is the biller already in the saved payee list?
questions.why: The screen displays your current bill pay payees alongside an '+ Add a payee' button, requiring you to decide if the biller is already set up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manage your payee list and personally verify that the correct new or existing biller is selected for the payment.
questions.check: Does the payee list already contain your biller?
questions.say_example: <PG&E> is already in your payees, so I'm using that one.

questions.question: Should I link the biller by logging into it, or add it by hand?
questions.why: The screen presents a choice between entering login credentials for an encrypted connection or clicking 'Add Biller Manually'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to share their biller login credentials with the bank or manually enter the payee details.
questions.check: Does the page offer to link the biller by logging into it, next to a manual option?
questions.say_example: It offers to log in to your <utility> account to pull bills. That means handing them your <utility> password. I'm adding it by hand instead. Say link if you'd rather.

questions.question: Which category is your biller under?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple options like 'Electric Utilities' and 'Water Utilities', so you must choose the correct classification to locate your specific payee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent navigate the categories means you lose direct oversight over how your specific utility provider is classified within the portal.
questions.check: Which category on the page matches the type of bill?
questions.say_example: Picked <Electric Utilities>

questions.question: Are you paying a company or a person?
questions.why: The interface requires categorizing the new payee by selecting either the 'Company' or 'Person' radio button under 'Who are you paying?'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over correctly categorizing the payee, which dictates what details are needed to set them up.
questions.check: Is 'Company' or 'Person' selected under 'Who are you paying?'
questions.say_example: The form is set to paying a person. <Your biller> is a company. Switching it.

questions.question: Which country's bills do you want to pay?
questions.why: The 'Pay Bills' menu requires selecting the specific country, such as Costa Rica or Mexico, where your biller is located.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the exact country for their bill payment, which could result in the agent being unable to locate the correct international payee.
questions.check: Which country is selected, and which country is the biller in?
questions.say_example: The country is set to <Mexico>. Your biller is in <Costa Rica>. Switching it.

questions.question: Which of the search results is the biller on your bill?
questions.why: Because the screen currently shows a loading spinner after typing the query, you must wait for the results to populate to ensure you select the correct, verified biller.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify that the correct official biller was selected from the search results rather than a similarly named but incorrect payee.
questions.check: Which search results share the biller's name, and what does each say it is - the standard bill, a prepaid load, a department?
questions.say_example: Several matches for <Chase>. <Card Services>, <Auto>, <Mortgage>. Which one is on your bill?

questions.question: Does the summary now show the company just picked?
questions.why: The radio button for COOPELESCA is selected, but the Transaction Summary panel still displays 'Compañía Nacional de Fuerza y Luz', indicating the interface may not have registered the change.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to catch a silent interface failure where their selection hasn't fully registered, potentially leading them to pay the wrong company.
questions.check: Does the summary panel name the same company as the selected radio button?
questions.say_example: I picked <COOPELESCA>, but the summary still says <the old company>. I'm re-selecting it before going on.

questions.question: Does the account number filled into the form match the saved payee?
questions.why: Confirming the pre-filled credit card number and email ensures the payment will be routed to the correct account without manual entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of personally verifying that the system has loaded the correct account details for your payee.
questions.check: Which fields on the payment form are prefilled, and does the account number match the saved payee?
questions.say_example: The form filled in the account ending <[account number]>. Your bill says <1553>. I'm fixing it.

questions.question: Do you want eBills from this payee sent here?
questions.why: The screen prompts to subscribe to eBills, which requires the last four digits of your SSN and a selection for receiving options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your billing preferences and whether your SSN is used to enroll in electronic statements.
questions.check: Does the page offer eBills for this payee, and what does it require to subscribe?
questions.say_example: It offers to bring this payee's bills here. That needs the last four of your SSN. I'm skipping it. Say yes if you want them.

questions.question: Does the vendor's eBill status now show as subscribed?
questions.why: Confirming the green 'Subscribed' badge ensures that future bills from this vendor will automatically appear in your portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that the eBill connection was successfully established.
questions.check: What does the eBill status badge for this vendor show?
questions.say_example: Saw the eBill badge read Subscribed for <vendor>

questions.question: Is the eBill actually on, when one screen says pending and the other says subscribed?
questions.why: The confirmation screen states eBills will be added once approved, but the vendor profile immediately shows a 'Subscribed' status with a past bill date, creating confusion about the actual setup status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating this loses the opportunity to investigate whether the eBill is truly active or if they still need to manually monitor for the next statement.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say the eBill is pending while the vendor page shows it subscribed?
questions.say_example: One screen says the eBill is pending. The other says it's on. Until a bill actually shows up here, watch for the paper one.

children.label: Enter the payee by hand
children.note: 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 in the form's order - on the wallets and on S-Pankki 3.5.2 is the payment form itself and the payee record is never saved. 3.5.3 where the platform standardizes the address (lpVy). 3.5.4 where offered, and after the payment on GCash. then 3.5.5.

questions.question: What name, mailing address, and phone does the add-payee form need from your bill?
questions.why: The 'Add a payee' screen requires the complete physical address to ensure the payment is routed to the correct destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that the payment is being sent to the exact, correct address for your biller.
questions.check: Which name, address, and phone fields on the add-payee form are required, and which are still empty?
questions.say_example: This payee isn't in their list, so it needs the name and mailing address from your bill. Read me the pay-to address on the statement.

questions.question: Does one of the names the form offers match the biller on your bill?
questions.why: The screen displayed a dropdown of previously entered names, requiring you to decide whether to select an existing contact or type a new one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over exactly who is added to your payee list, risking a payment being sent to the wrong person.
questions.check: Does the name field offer previously entered names, and does one match the biller?
questions.say_example: The form offers <a name> from a past payee. It matches your bill, so I'm using it.

questions.question: Does the payee name on the form match the pay-to name on your bill?
questions.why: The speaker warns that companies often use DBAs, and entering the wrong name will cause the paper check to be rejected by the payee's bank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to verify the exact legal or DBA name required by the payee, risking a bounced or uncashable check.
questions.check: Does the payee name on the form match the pay-to name printed on the bill?
questions.say_example: The check will be printed to <the name typed>. Your bill says pay to <a different name>. A wrong name means the check bounces. I'm using the name on the bill.

questions.question: Is the payee's phone number typed in the format the form wants?
questions.why: The speaker explicitly notes that you must include the "hash marks" (dashes) between the numbers when entering the company's phone number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to ensure the phone number is formatted correctly according to the system's specific requirements, which might cause validation errors.
questions.check: Does the phone field show a format error?
questions.say_example: Re-entered the phone with dashes

questions.question: Is the name typed the way the statement prints it, in the order the form wants?
questions.why: The physical billing statement shows a specific name format, so you must carefully extract and enter just the surname and first name exactly as printed to avoid payment errors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct name from your physical billing statement is interpreted and formatted accurately in the app.
questions.check: Does the name field match the name printed on the statement, in the order the form asks for?
questions.say_example: The form wants surname first. Your statement says <surname, first name>, so I'm entering it that way.

questions.question: What account or customer number from your bill does the form ask for?
questions.why: The 'Add a payee' screen includes an 'Account number (recommended)' field to ensure the payment is accurately routed to your specific account with the biller.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of personally verifying that their exact account number is entered to prevent a misdirected payment.
questions.check: Which account, customer, or reference number does the form ask for, and where does the page say it appears on the bill?
questions.say_example: It needs your account number with <the biller>. The page shows where it sits on the bill, top right under <customer code>. Read it to me.

questions.question: What are the vendor's bank routing and account numbers?
questions.why: The screen requires the vendor's 9-digit routing number and account number to save their bank details for future payments.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the correct routing and account numbers are being saved for this specific vendor.
questions.check: Which bank account fields does the form require for the payee - routing, account, IBAN - and does it offer to let the vendor enter their own?
questions.say_example: The form wants <the vendor's> bank details. Routing and account number, or you can have them enter it by email. Read me the numbers from the invoice, or say invite.

questions.question: What reference number from the invoice goes in the reference field?
questions.why: The invoice displays a specific 'Viitenumero' (reference number) that must be entered into the corresponding field without spaces to ensure the business correctly attributes the payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually verify that the exact reference number from the invoice is chosen over a generic message and formatted correctly.
questions.check: Does the form have a reference number field, and what reference does the invoice show?
questions.say_example: There's a reference field. The invoice shows <number>. I'm entering it without spaces, so the payment lands on your account.

questions.question: Will you type the full card number in yourself?
questions.why: The screen explicitly prompts for a 16-digit credit card number to identify the funding account for the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually select and verify the specific credit card used to fund the payment.
questions.check: Does the form ask for a full card number?
questions.say_example: It wants the full card number. I don't take card numbers. Type it in, and tell me when it's done.

questions.question: Is your email in the receipt field?
questions.why: Entering an accurate email address ensures you receive a digital receipt for your records once the payment is complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose which email address receives the payment confirmation or whether to provide one at all.
questions.check: Does the receipt email field contain your email?
questions.say_example: Entered <email> for the receipt

questions.question: Is the address the site suggests the same place as the one typed?
questions.why: The screen asks you to confirm a standardized pay-to address before saving the payee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the system's suggested address is correct for your specific biller.
questions.check: Does the standardized address the page recommends differ from what was typed?
questions.say_example: The site corrected the address. The ZIP typed puts it in <Idaho>. Its suggestion is <the full address>. I'm using that.

questions.question: On what day of the month should the app remind you to pay this bill?
questions.why: The 'Edit Biller' screen provides a 'Remind Me Every' dropdown list to select a specific day for recurring monthly notifications.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strategically time the reminder based on your personal cash flow and preferred buffer around the actual due date.
questions.check: What day is selected in the 'Remind Me Every' dropdown?
questions.say_example: Left the reminder on <the 1st>

questions.question: Do you want this amount saved for future payments to this biller?
questions.why: The 'Edit Biller' screen pre-filled the optional amount field with the last transaction's value, which needs to be cleared if the bill fluctuates monthly.

questions.why: The final receipt shows the payment was processed using a credit or debit card instead of the rewards points selected on the payment gateway.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might fail to notice this discrepancy, resulting in an unexpected charge to your card instead of using your rewards points.
questions.check: Does the payment method on the receipt match the one selected?
questions.say_example: The receipt says it charged your <card>. You picked <rewards points>. The points weren't used.

questions.question: Is the page warning this payment would overdraw the account?
questions.why: If the payment exceeds the available balance, the bank might charge an overdraft fee or reject the payment entirely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to switch funding accounts or lower the payment amount to avoid costly overdraft fees or a bounced payment.
questions.check: Does the review page show an insufficient funds or overdraft warning?
questions.say_example: The page warns this would overdraw <checking>. That's a fee on top. I'm holding.

questions.question: Is the page warning the amount is over a daily or bill-pay limit?
questions.why: Large bills (like property taxes or tuition) might hit a bank's security limit, requiring the payment to be split across multiple days or authorized differently.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to adjust the payment amount or contact the bank to raise the limit before the transaction is outright blocked.
questions.check: Does the review page warn the amount exceeds a daily or bill-pay limit?
questions.say_example: This is over the <5,000> daily limit. The bank won't send it in one go. It can go as <two> payments on different days.

questions.question: Are the amount, payee, account, dates, and fee on the review screen right?
questions.why: The screen presents a final review step with a 'Schedule' button to confirm the transaction and an 'Edit' link to make changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your final chance to personally verify the payment amount, date, and funding account before the funds are committed.
questions.check: What amount, payee, funding account, fee, send date, and delivery date does the review screen show?
questions.say_example: Ready to pay. <217.03> to <PG&E>, from checking ending <[account number]>. Arrives <June 12>. No fee. Press to pay, or say change.

questions.question: Was Submit actually pressed, or did the page move on without it?
questions.why: Navigating to the Accounts tab without clicking 'Submit Payment(s)' means the $50 transaction was abandoned and never processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user is left with an unpaid bill and a false sense of security, potentially leading to late fees or service interruption.
questions.check: Is a confirmation showing, or is the payment form still on screen with the submit button unpressed?
questions.say_example: I left the page without pressing Submit. Nothing was paid. I'm going back to the review screen, and I'll ask before pressing it.

questions.question: Is the pay button greyed out because a field has an error?
questions.why: If a field is formatted incorrectly, the submit button often turns gray without an explicit error popup, requiring the user to scan the form for red borders.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual cue that the form is incomplete, which might cause the agent to fail silently or get stuck trying to click a disabled button.
questions.check: Is the submit button disabled, and which field shows a red outline or error?
questions.say_example: The pay button is greyed out. The <phone> field is outlined red. Fixing that first.

questions.question: Will you read in the code from your security card yourself?
questions.why: The screen prompts for a specific passcode corresponding to column A and row 00 on your physical security card to authorize the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing your physical security card or its codes, which compromises the multi-factor authentication protecting your bank account.
questions.check: What does the page ask for before it sends - a code from a security card, a text code, a PIN, or a card-check popup - and which cell or number does it name?
questions.say_example: To send it, the bank wants the code from your security card, column <A> row <00>. Read it to me, or type it yourself.

children.label: Verify the payment
children.note: 9.1 on every completed keeper. 9.2 where a receipt can be kept or arrives elsewhere. 9.3 and 9.4 as the after-check - 9.3 moves at once on the transfers and the wallets and not at all on the scheduled checks; 9.4 stays put until the next business day and the platform says so. 9.5 where a scheduled, pending or history list exists. 9.6 never happens in the corpus. 9.7 loops back to 2 - three times in 8n6j, and 4uIk sets up next month's pass.

questions.question: Is the payment confirmed and do you have the reference number?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Payment Received' message along with a reference number and posting timeline, which serves as your official proof of payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate opportunity to screenshot or save the specific reference number for your own personal records in case of a billing dispute.
questions.check: What does the confirmation say - amount, payee, reference number, and when it posts - and is it a page that stays, or a message that vanished?
questions.say_example: Paid. <2,241.04> to <the biller>. Reference <number>. It posts in <three business days>.

questions.question: Do the amount and date on the confirmation match what you approved?
questions.why: Checking that the final confirmation screen reflects the exact amount and date you submitted ensures the system processed your payment correctly without unexpected changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to immediately catch and document a system error if the processed payment differs from what was authorized.
questions.check: Do the amount and date on the confirmation match the amount and date on the review screen?
questions.say_example: The confirmation says <10>. We authorized <30>. The scheduled list shows <10> too. Only <10> is going. I'm not sending anything else on my own. Tell me if you want the other <20> sent.

questions.question: Did an error page come up after submit instead of a confirmation?
questions.why: If the portal times out, the payment might be in limbo, requiring you to check your bank or contact support rather than just trying again and risking a double charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that the payment status is unknown, which dictates whether they should wait, check their bank, or retry.
questions.check: Did an error or timeout page appear after submit instead of a confirmation?
questions.say_example: The page errored after I pressed pay. The money may or may not have gone. I'm not pressing again. Checking the payments list first.

questions.question: Does the confirmation say the payment is held or pending review?
questions.why: Fraud algorithms sometimes flag unusual payments (e.g., a new large payee or an out-of-pattern amount) for manual bank review, delaying the processing indefinitely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their payment is delayed and might require them to call the bank's fraud department to release the funds.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say the payment is pending review or held?
questions.say_example: It went through, but the bank is holding it for review. No date given. It may not arrive by <the due date>.

questions.question: Do you want to download and save a copy of the payment receipt?
questions.why: The confirmation screen provides a reference number and an option to save the receipt, which serves as proof of payment while the transaction processes over the next three business days.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate, personal possession of the downloaded receipt image on their own device for their financial records.
questions.check: Does the confirmation offer a receipt to save or download?
questions.say_example: Saved the receipt to <Downloads>

questions.question: Does the confirmation say a receipt was emailed to you?
questions.why: Reviewing the GCash email receipt ensures the payment amount of PHP 2241.04 and the biller SOCOTECO1 were processed correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of personally verifying the email receipt to confirm the exact payment details were recorded correctly.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say a receipt was sent by email, and to which address?
questions.say_example: Noted the confirmation says a receipt went to <email>

questions.question: Is the new checking balance the old one minus the payments made?
questions.why: Verifying that the initial balance of $3,746.76 decreased by exactly the sum of the three payments to $3,692.27 ensures no extra fees or errors occurred during processing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the mathematical certainty of independently verifying that your account was debited for the exact intended amounts without any unexpected charges.
questions.check: Does the new balance equal the old balance minus the payments made?
questions.say_example: Checking was <3,746.76>. Three payments should leave <3,692.27>. It shows <3,680>. That's <12> more than the payments. Something else came out.

questions.question: Now that this is paid, is the autopay still going to pay it again?
questions.why: The screen displayed a warning about an upcoming automatic minimum payment, which could result in an unintended double charge if not addressed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the financial assurance that they will not be double-charged by an overlapping automatic payment.
questions.check: After the payment, does the page still show an automatic payment scheduled for this bill?
questions.say_example: Autopay is still set for <the 28th>. The bill may get paid twice. You can turn it off under autopay.

questions.question: Does the bill's balance now show the payment?
questions.why: Noticing that the checking balance decreased while the credit card balance remained unchanged helps you understand the processing delay for the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of seeing exactly how and when your account balances update after a payment is submitted.
questions.check: Does the bill's balance or amount due now reflect the payment?
questions.say_example: Checked the card balance, still <217.03>, payment not posted yet

questions.question: Is the new payment in the scheduled payments list with the right amount and date?
questions.why: Checking the scheduled payments list confirms that the system successfully registered the transaction for the correct date and amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that the payment is officially queued in the system and matches your intended details.
questions.check: Does the scheduled payments list show the new payment with the right amount and date?
questions.say_example: Found the payment in the scheduled list, <50> to <Qbk Accounting> on <June 12>

questions.question: Until when can this scheduled payment be cancelled?
questions.why: Checking the payment details confirms that no unexpected processing fees were applied and identifies the exact window available to cancel the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate peace of mind of personally verifying the zero-dollar fee and knowing exactly how long you have to cancel the payment.
questions.check: What does the scheduled payment's detail page say about cancelling, and until when?
questions.say_example: You can cancel this until <it's sent on the 20th>. After that it's paid.
